Field description: If HED tags are used:
The version of the HED schema used to validate HED tags for study.
May include a single schema or a base schema and one or more library schema.

Field description: Used to specify the locations and relevant attributes of all source datasets (BIDS or not).
Valid keys in each object include `"URL"`, `"DOI"` (see
[URI](SPEC_ROOT/common-principles.md#uniform-resource-indicator)), and
`"Version"` with
[string](https://www.w3schools.com/js/js_json_datatypes.asp)
values.

Field description: [URI](SPEC_ROOT/common-principles.md#uniform-resource-indicator)
of the corresponding [CogPO](http://www.cogpo.org/) term.

Field description: (If used)
A method for reducing the number of independent channels by combining in
analog the signals from multiple coil elements.
There are typically different default modes when using un-accelerated or
accelerated (for example, `"GRAPPA"`, `"SENSE"`) imaging.

Field description: Almost all fMRI studies using phased-array coils use root-sum-of-squares
(rSOS) combination, but other methods exist.
The image reconstruction is changed by the coil combination method
(as for the matrix coil mode above),
so anything non-standard should be reported.
Field description: A general description of the pulse sequence used for the scan.

Field description: Boolean stating if the image saved has been corrected for gradient
nonlinearities by the scanner sequence.

Field description: The direction where only partial Fourier information was collected.
Corresponds to [DICOM Tag 0018, 9036](http://www.dicomlookup.com/dicomtags/(0018,9036))
`Partial Fourier Direction`.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

analog the signals from multiple coil elements.
There are typically different default modes when using un-accelerated or
accelerated (for example, `"GRAPPA"`, `"SENSE"`) imaging.

Field description: Almost all fMRI studies using phased-array coils use root-sum-of-squares
(rSOS) combination, but other methods exist.
The image reconstruction is changed by the coil combination method
(as for the matrix coil mode above),
so anything non-standard should be reported.
Field description: A general description of the pulse sequence used for the scan.

Field description: Boolean stating if the image saved has been corrected for gradient
nonlinearities by the scanner sequence.

Field description: The direction where only partial Fourier information was collected.
Corresponds to [DICOM Tag 0018, 9036](http://www.dicomlookup.com/dicomtags/(0018,9036))
`Partial Fourier Direction`.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.

slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: (If used)
A method for reducing the number of independent channels by combining in
analog the signals from multiple coil elements.
There are typically different default modes when using un-accelerated or
accelerated (for example, `"GRAPPA"`, `"SENSE"`) imaging.

Field description: Almost all fMRI studies using phased-array coils use root-sum-of-squares
(rSOS) combination, but other methods exist.
The image reconstruction is changed by the coil combination method
(as for the matrix coil mode above),
so anything non-standard should be reported.
Field description: A general description of the pulse sequence used for the scan.

Field description: Boolean stating if the image saved has been corrected for gradient
nonlinearities by the scanner sequence.

Field description: The direction where only partial Fourier information was collected.
Corresponds to [DICOM Tag 0018, 9036](http://www.dicomlookup.com/dicomtags/(0018,9036))
`Partial Fourier Direction`.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

acquisition.

the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.

dimension (see below).

it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.

the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.

Field description: The time at which each slice was acquired within each volume (frame) of the
acquisition.
Slice timing is not slice order -- rather, it is a list of times containing
the time (in seconds) of each slice acquisition in relation to the beginning
of volume acquisition.
The list goes through the slices along the slice axis in the slice encoding
dimension (see below).
Note that to ensure the proper interpretation of the `"SliceTiming"` field,
it is important to check if the OPTIONAL `SliceEncodingDirection` exists.
In particular, if `"SliceEncodingDirection"` is negative,
the entries in `"SliceTiming"` are defined in reverse order with respect to the
slice axis, such that the final entry in the `"SliceTiming"` list is the time
of acquisition of slice 0. Without this parameter slice time correction will
not be possible.
